speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; please tell me, did this dizziness start while you were at rest or during activity, and do you feel any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or tinnitus?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. The fact that your symptoms lasted only about three minutes and resolved completely suggests a transient event; were you standing or lying down when this started, and did you experience any double vision, slurred speech, or weakness in your limbs at that time?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical picture of brief, spontaneous vertigo episodes lasting minutes without auditory symptoms, headache, or focal neurological deficits is most consistent with this condition. Given the high probability, do you require a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis?
